question: Walking at (2)/(3) of his normal speed, Abhijeet is 28 minutes late in reaching. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his destination is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **distance** is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time**.

Speed ratio (Usual : New) = 1 : 2/3 = 3 : 2

Time ratio (Usual : New) = 2 : 3

Difference in time ratio = 3 − 2 = 1 unit → 28 minutes

Usual time = 2 units = 2 × 28 minutes = 56 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 56 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/742d2be54526e17d616d4e54ce41ebc1e07b66717388d7dce7234f6d20025c93.png] 

**Given:**

New Speed (S₂) = 2/3 of Usual Speed (S₁)

Time difference (Δt) = 28 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Speed × Time = Distance

Usual Time (T) = [Late time × Numerator] ÷ [Difference between Numerator and Denominator]

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let usual speed be S and usual time be T.

⇒ New speed = (2/3)S and New time = T + 28

⇒ S × T = (2/3)S × (T + 28)

⇒ T = (2/3)(T + 28)

⇒ 3T = 2T + 56

⇒ T = 56 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 56 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality Rule

If speed becomes a/b of its original value, then time becomes b/a of its original value provided the distance is constant.

Average Speed

For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

Same direction: (S₁ − S₂) | Opposite direction: (S₁ + S₂).</p
